hero.headline: Bus crash on Virginia highway kills 5, injures dozens
hero.body:
A bus crashed into several vehicles near a work zone on Interstate 95 in Stafford County, Virginia, killing five people and injuring dozens more. The crash occurred on the southbound lanes of the highway.

Two children and three adults died in the collision. State police identified the bus driver but have not released the name publicly. The number of injured passengers has been described as in the dozens, though an exact count was not provided.

A survivor of the crash told reporters the bus was traveling at high speed before impact. The crash happened in an area designated as a work zone, where traffic patterns may have been altered for road construction or maintenance.

Authorities have not disclosed what caused the bus to plow into the other vehicles or whether any charges will be filed. The investigation into the circumstances of the crash is ongoing.

Interstate 95 is a major north-south highway along the East Coast, connecting cities from Maine to Florida. Stafford County sits between Washington, D.C., and Richmond, Virginia, making the stretch of highway heavily trafficked by commuters and long-distance travelers.

The crash ranks among the deadlier vehicle accidents in Virginia in recent years. Emergency responders transported the injured to area hospitals, though the severity of their conditions has not been disclosed.

Police have not indicated whether mechanical failure, weather conditions, or driver error contributed to the collision. The work zone where the crash occurred typically features reduced speed limits and lane restrictions to protect construction workers and drivers.

cards.headline: Trump Delays Decision on Iran Cease-Fire Proposal
cards.teaser: The president met with aides for two hours but did not announce a final determination on a potential cease-fire extension.
cards.body:
President Trump met with advisers for two hours at the White House to discuss a possible cease-fire extension with Iran. A senior administration official confirmed the meeting took place, though no decision was announced following the talks.

US and Iranian officials have agreed on a framework for a potential deal. Trump had indicated on social media that he was preparing to make a final determination on the proposal.

cards.headline: Ukraine Prepares for Major Russian Attacks Within 24 Hours
cards.teaser: President Zelenskyy said Ukraine is bracing for significant strikes by Russia in the coming day.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Russia is preparing major new attacks on Ukraine within the next 24 hours. The announcement prompted an emergency meeting at the UN Security Council to discuss the escalating threat.

During overnight strikes on Ukraine, a Russian drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania, injuring two people. A Russian official subsequently warned Europe to prepare for additional drone incidents as attacks continue.

cards.headline: Oil prices drop as US and Iran move closer to agreement
cards.teaser: Oil prices fell as investors evaluated signs of progress toward a potential agreement between the United States and Iran.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell on Thursday following reports of a potential breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations. The tentative agreement to extend a ceasefire, pending approval, prompted global markets to reassess energy outlooks as investors weighed the implications of reduced Middle East tensions.

Oil experienced its largest monthly decline since 2020. The potential deal contributed to market volatility as traders evaluated how a diplomatic resolution could affect global energy supplies and pricing.

cards.headline: White House proposes rule allowing cancellation of federal research grants at any time
cards.body:
The federal government proposed new funding rules that would allow officials to cancel research grants at any time. The proposed changes also make peer review optional for grant applications and would require political staff to screen grants for forbidden topics.

The rules represent a shift in how federal research funding operates. For decades, peer review has been the standard process for evaluating scientific grant proposals, with experts in the field assessing the merit and feasibility of proposed research.

Under the proposed system, political appointees would gain authority to review grant applications before approval. The screening process would check for topics deemed off-limits by the administration. The nature of these forbidden topics was not specified in the available information.

The ability to cancel grants at any time marks a departure from current practice. Research grants typically run for fixed terms, with cancellation generally limited to cases of fraud or failure to meet stated objectives. The proposed rules would remove these constraints, giving officials broad discretion to terminate funding.

The optional peer review provision would eliminate the requirement that expert scientists evaluate grant proposals. Peer review has long been considered a safeguard against political interference in research, ensuring that funding decisions rest on scientific merit rather than ideology or politics.

Research institutions rely heavily on federal grants to fund scientific work. The government supports research across fields including medicine, physics, climate science, and technology development. Changes to grant procedures could affect how universities and research centers plan and conduct long-term studies.

The proposal comes as federal science agencies face broader changes to their operations and priorities. How the new rules would interact with existing grant commitments and ongoing research projects remains to be determined. The proposed rules would need to go through a formal comment period before taking effect.

cards.headline: SEC proposes repeal of climate disclosure rule for companies
cards.teaser: The Securities and Exchange Commission moved to eliminate a rule requiring companies to report greenhouse gas emissions and climate risks.
cards.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission proposed repealing a rule requiring companies to disclose their greenhouse gas emissions and climate-related financial risks to investors. The rule, implemented during the Biden administration under SEC Chair Gary Gensler, aimed to give investors standardized information about how companies manage climate risks.

The proposed repeal marks a shift in regulatory priorities under the current administration's approach to environmental and business policy.

cards.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes during testing, threatening NASA moon program delays
cards.body:
A New Glenn rocket operated by Blue Origin exploded on the launchpad at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night, destroying the launch facility and threatening NASA's ambitious timeline for lunar exploration. The massive fireball erupted seconds after the start of a scheduled static fire test at 9pm ET, with the orange glow visible more than 115 miles away in Fort Pierce.

The explosion comes just days after NASA announced that Blue Origin had won a contract to launch the first of three planned uncrewed lunar missions this year to begin construction of a $20 billion moon base. NASA's administrator Jared Isaacman emphasized that the agency would conduct a full evaluation of how the incident affects the timeline for the moon program.

"Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult," Isaacman wrote on social media. "We will work with our partners to support a thorough investigation of this anomaly, assess near-term mission impacts, and get back to launching rockets."

Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos confirmed that all employees were safe and uninjured. In a statement on social media, Bezos acknowledged it was "a very rough day" but expressed confidence the company would recover. "It's too early to know the root cause but we're already working to find it. We'll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying. It's worth it," he said.

The New Glenn rocket is central to Blue Origin's role in NASA's Artemis program, which aims to return astronauts to the lunar surface for the first time since 1972. The rocket is intended to launch lunar landers to the moon, including the landers that will carry astronauts to the surface during the Artemis IV mission planned for 2028. Blue Origin is also competing with SpaceX to provide a lunar lander for that mission.

The explosion represents the latest setback for Blue Origin as it attempts to compete with SpaceX for lucrative NASA contracts. Last month, a payload from the third flight of the New Glenn ended up in the wrong orbit, leading the Federal Aviation Administration to temporarily ground the rocket. Thursday's static fire test was the first since the FAA cleared the vehicle to return to flight the previous week.

Shockwaves from the explosion were felt across Florida's Space Coast, with residents in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach reporting that their homes shook. Launch Complex 36, located at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, has been used for rocket launches since the 1960s. Blue Origin had been preparing the facility specifically for New Glenn operations.

Emergency officials reported no threat from fumes or other hazards following the explosion. Flames were still burning at the launchpad more than two hours after the incident.

hero.headline: Russian Drone Strikes Romanian Apartment Building, Injuring Two Civilians
hero.body:
A Russian drone hit an apartment building in Romania, injuring two civilians in what officials described as the first such attack to harm residents of the NATO member country. The strike occurred near the Ukrainian border.

Romania is a member of NATO, and the security alliance condemned what it called Russia's recklessness. The incident sharply escalated tensions between the military alliance and Moscow.

A Russian official warned Europe to prepare for additional drone incidents following the Romania episode. The official stated that the peaceful sleep is over, signaling potential future incidents across the continent.

Drones from the war in Ukraine have crossed into Romanian territory before, but this marked the first time civilians were injured. The proximity to Ukraine has made Romania vulnerable to such incursions as the conflict continues.

NATO member states issued statements condemning Russia after the drone crashed into the residential building. The alliance characterized the incident as part of a pattern of dangerous behavior by Russian forces near NATO borders.

The strike adds to growing concerns about the spillover effects of the Ukraine conflict on neighboring countries. Romania shares a border with Ukraine and has been monitoring airspace violations throughout the war.

Russian forces have used drones extensively in attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure and military targets. The devices have occasionally strayed or been directed beyond Ukraine's borders, creating diplomatic incidents.

The two injured civilians received medical treatment following the strike. Romanian officials have not released details about the extent of their injuries or the damage to the apartment building.

This incident represents a direct impact on NATO territory from Russian military operations. The alliance has repeatedly stated that an attack on one member is an attack on all, though officials have not indicated whether this drone strike meets that threshold.

The episode comes as tensions remain high between Russia and Western nations over the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. NATO countries have provided substantial military and economic support to Ukraine while avoiding direct military confrontation with Russia.

cards.headline: Trump Delays Decision on Iran Cease-Fire Proposal
cards.teaser: The president met with aides for two hours but did not announce a final determination on a potential cease-fire extension.
cards.body:
President Trump met with advisers for two hours at the White House to discuss a possible cease-fire extension with Iran. A senior administration official confirmed the meeting took place, though no decision was announced following the talks.

US and Iranian officials have agreed on a framework for a potential deal. Trump had indicated on social media that he was preparing to make a final determination on the proposal.

cards.headline: Iranian Hard-Liners Push Back Against US Deal
cards.teaser: A small but vocal faction in Iran has used rallies and state media to oppose ongoing negotiations with the United States.
cards.body:
A political fight is unfolding in Iran as hard-liners attempt to derail potential negotiations with the United States. The faction has organized rallies and used state media along with private and public statements to undermine the talks.

The opposition represents a minority within Iranian politics but has maintained a loud presence in the debate. Their efforts come as officials from both countries work toward a potential agreement on a cease-fire framework.

cards.headline: UN Adds Israel and Russia to Sexual Violence Blacklist
cards.teaser: Israeli and Russian forces have been placed on the United Nations list of parties that commit sexual violence in conflict zones.
cards.body:
The United Nations added both Israel and Russia to its blacklist for sexual violence in conflict, marking the first time Israel has appeared on the list. The designation follows a UN report documenting sexual abuse by security forces in both countries, including the rape of male detainees.

The UN verified sexual abuse of 31 Palestinian men, women and children from Gaza and the occupied West Bank between 2023 and 2025. According to the report, Israeli forces committed repeated gang-rapes and used sexual violence as a form of torture. Both governments have blocked UN investigators from conducting full investigations.

cards.headline: Ukraine Prepares for Major Russian Attacks Within 24 Hours
cards.teaser: President Zelenskyy said Ukraine is bracing for significant strikes by Russia in the coming day.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Russia is preparing major new attacks on Ukraine within the next 24 hours. The announcement prompted an emergency meeting at the UN Security Council to discuss the escalating threat.

During overnight strikes on Ukraine, a Russian drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania, injuring two people. A Russian official subsequently warned Europe to prepare for additional drone incidents as attacks continue.

cards.headline: Ghana Parliament Passes Bill Criminalizing LGBTQ Promotion
cards.teaser: Lawmakers approved legislation that would make promoting LGBTQ activities a criminal offense, an official said.
cards.body:
Ghana's parliament passed a bill that criminalizes the promotion of LGBTQ activities and targets LGBTQ people directly. The legislation now awaits the president's signature to become law.

The bill faced opposition from minority lawmakers but passed with support from the majority. Supporters characterized it as protecting traditional values, while critics say it violates human rights and targets a vulnerable community.

cards.headline: First Survivor Rescued From Flooded Laos Cave After Nine Days
cards.teaser: Rescuers brought out one of five men trapped in a flooded cavern for over a week.
cards.body:
The first of seven men trapped in a flooded cave in Laos for over a week has been rescued after a perilous operation. Divers navigated narrow, water-filled tunnels filled with sharp rocks and collapse hazards to extract the survivor to safety.

Four of the men remain in a chamber about 300 metres from the cave entrance, where they were discovered huddled together on a rocky ledge. Two others are still missing. An international team of rescue divers, including some who participated in the 2018 Thai cave rescue, continues efforts to bring the remaining trapped men to safety.

cards.headline: Judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center
cards.teaser: A judge ruled that President Trump's name must be taken off the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington.
cards.body:
A federal judge has ordered that President Trump's name be removed from the Kennedy Center, striking down a renaming of the performing arts venue. The court also blocked the center's proposed two-year closure for extensive renovations.

Trump responded by saying he has "no interest" in the Kennedy Center following the judge's decision, attacking the ruling online.

cards.headline: ICE agent charged in Minneapolis shooting arrested in Texas
cards.teaser: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent wanted for a shooting during an immigration operation in Minneapolis was captured in Texas.
cards.body:
Christian Castro, a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent, was arrested Friday in Texas following charges filed by Minneapolis prosecutors. Castro was wanted in connection with the shooting of a Venezuelan man during an immigration enforcement operation in January.

The agent faces charges of assault and falsely reporting a crime. His arrest came 11 days after prosecutors formally charged him, following the emergence of video evidence related to the non-fatal shooting.

cards.headline: Three climbers dead, one rescued after fall on Mount McKinley
cards.teaser: Three mountaineers died after falling from 18,200 feet on Alaska's Mount McKinley, while a fourth was rescued alive.
cards.body:
Rescue crews recovered three bodies and rescued one climber following a fall on Mount McKinley near a treacherous pass at 18,200 feet elevation. The surviving climber was transported off the mountain.

Mount McKinley, also known as Denali, is Alaska's tallest peak and one of the world's most challenging climbs. Authorities launched a search and rescue operation after receiving reports of the incident.

cards.headline: Judge blocks payouts from Trump's $1.776 billion settlement fund
cards.teaser: A federal judge temporarily halted disbursements from President Trump's fund meant to compensate alleged victims of government overreach.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Virginia issued a temporary order blocking the Trump administration from transferring money into a $1.8 billion fund designed to settle claims of government weaponization. The order prevents the government from taking any further action in creating or operating the fund while legal challenges proceed.

US District Judge Leonie Brinkema's ruling aims to ensure no funds are irreversibly disbursed from the Anti-Weaponization fund while the case continues. The order came as part of an ongoing lawsuit challenging the fund's legality and structure.

cards.headline: Airlines warn of chaos if administration restricts international flights
cards.teaser: Major airlines and business groups cautioned that limiting international flights could cause widespread travel disruption.
cards.body:
Airlines and business organizations warned of potential chaos if the administration moves forward with plans to restrict international flight operations at certain airports. The concerns center on a proposal to pull customs officers from Newark airport as part of a broader dispute over sanctuary jurisdictions.

The travel industry urged the administration not to curb international flights in its feud with cities that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement. Airlines warned that removing customs personnel or restricting international operations could strand passengers and disrupt global commerce.

cards.headline: Man admits selling toxic chemicals online to people who died by suicide
cards.teaser: Kenneth Law pleaded guilty to charges of aiding suicides after selling toxic substances online to buyers around the world.
cards.body:
Kenneth Law, a Canadian man, has pleaded guilty to 14 counts of assisting suicide. He sold lethal chemicals online and mailed "suicide packets" containing poison and instructions to more than 100 people across dozens of countries, including Canada, the UK, the US, Italy, Australia and New Zealand.

Law appeared in court in Newmarket, Ontario, after prosecutors withdrew 14 murder charges. Families of victims in Britain, where 79 deaths have been linked to substances he sold, are calling for him to face charges there as well. Sentencing is scheduled for September.

cards.headline: Dell stock surges 32% in best day ever as AI server revenue climbs
cards.teaser: Dell shares jumped 32% in the company's best single-day performance on record after reporting strong AI server sales.
cards.body:
Dell Technologies shares soared 32% in what marked the best trading day in the company's history. The surge came after the company reported strong revenue from AI server sales, reflecting growing demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure.

The stock rally added $34 billion to founder Michael Dell's personal fortune, making him wealthier than Mark Zuckerberg. Other server manufacturers also saw their shares rise following Dell's results. Jim Cramer noted that Dell's performance sets up an important week for AI-related stocks.

cards.teaser: The Securities and Exchange Commission moved to eliminate a rule requiring companies to report greenhouse gas emissions and climate risks.

cards.teaser: Oil prices fell as investors evaluated signs of progress toward a potential agreement between the United States and Iran.
cards.body:

Oil experienced its largest monthly decline since 2020. The potential deal contributed to market volatility as traders evaluated how a diplomatic resolution could affect global energy supplies and pricing.

cards.headline: Universal Music rejects Bill Ackman's $64 billion takeover offer
cards.teaser: Universal Music Group declined a $64 billion takeover proposal from Bill Ackman's Pershing Square, calling the offer too low.
cards.body:
Universal Music Group has turned down a takeover proposal from billionaire investor Bill Ackman's Pershing Square, valuing the company at $64-65 billion. The music giant stated that the bid significantly undervalues its business.

A major shareholder backed Universal's rejection of the offer. Pershing Square had aimed to acquire the Amsterdam-listed company, which operates music labels and holds rights across multiple genres worldwide.

cards.headline: Stock markets close at record highs with ninth straight weekly gain for S&P 500
cards.teaser: Major US stock indexes reached fresh record highs, with the S&P 500 posting its ninth consecutive weekly gain.
cards.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all closed at record levels, capping a winning month for equity markets. The S&P 500 extended its streak to nine straight weeks of gains, while the Nasdaq rose 8% over the month.

Technology stocks led the rally, with Dell's 32% surge providing significant momentum. The gains came as investors weighed developments including potential US-Iran negotiations and continued strength in artificial intelligence-related companies.

cards.headline: Train fire at Penn Station injures five, disrupts rail service
cards.teaser: A maintenance train fire near Penn Station injured five people and caused widespread delays during rush hour.
cards.body:
A fire on a maintenance train near Penn Station injured five people and disrupted service for Amtrak, NJ Transit, and Long Island Rail Road commuters. The incident occurred during evening rush hour, causing delays and cancellations across multiple rail lines.

Amtrak suspended service through Penn Station as crews worked to address the fire in the tunnel. The Metropolitan Transportation Authority described tunnel repairs as a chronic problem. The fire added to ongoing concerns about infrastructure maintenance at the busy transit hub.

cards.headline: Space Force awards SpaceX $6.45 billion in contracts ahead of public offering
cards.teaser: The contracts come as the company prepares to go public and disclosed that government work accounted for one-fifth of its 2025 revenue.
cards.body:
SpaceX received $6.45 billion in contracts from the Space Force, marking a significant boost to the company's government revenue ahead of its initial public offering. The aerospace company disclosed in its IPO filing that government contracts already accounted for one-fifth of its 2025 revenue, demonstrating the importance of these partnerships to its business model.

These new Space Force awards will expand SpaceX's existing government revenue stream as the company prepares to transition to public markets. The contracts underscore the military's continued reliance on SpaceX for national security space capabilities.

cards.headline: Kenyan court blocks US plan to relocate Ebola-exposed Americans to Kenya
cards.teaser: The ruling halts the Trump administration's proposal to move Americans exposed to Ebola to Kenya instead of specialized US facilities.
cards.body:
A Kenyan court has blocked the Trump administration's plan to establish a quarantine and treatment center in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola. The facility was intended to house U.S. citizens who came into contact with the virus during the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, rather than allowing them to return to the United States.

Some health experts have criticized the approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning home could hinder treatment efforts. The U.S. has existing specialized facilities designed specifically for managing Ebola exposures and quarantine within its own borders.

cards.headline: FCC warns broadcasters to follow orders or face ABC-style punishment
cards.teaser: The Trump administration's FCC issued a warning to all television broadcasters following its action against ABC.
cards.body:
The Federal Communications Commission under the Trump administration warned all broadcasters to follow orders or face punishment similar to what ABC received. The warning comes after the FCC took action against the network.

ABC stated that the FCC granted early license renewals for all its stations, a move the network called unprecedented and lacking legitimate purpose. The company characterized the early renewals as having no valid regulatory justification.

cards.headline: Authorities dismantle botnet controlling more than 17 million devices
cards.teaser: The massive botnet was reportedly connected to a Russia-based residential proxy network operation.
cards.body:
Law enforcement dismantled a botnet that had compromised more than 17 million devices. The network of infected computers and other internet-connected equipment represents one of the larger botnets taken down in recent years.

The botnet was reportedly tied to a residential proxy network based in Russia. Residential proxy networks route internet traffic through compromised home devices, allowing operators to mask their online activities and locations.

cards.headline: Texas measles outbreak analysis reveals one in five cases required hospitalization
cards.teaser: The outbreak data shows the dangers posed by measles, with most hospitalized patients developing complications.
cards.body:
Analysis of a measles outbreak in Texas found that about one in five cases required hospitalization. The data illustrates the serious health risks posed by the highly contagious virus.

Most of the hospitalized patients developed complications from their measles infections. The findings come as public health officials track measles cases across the country and work to prevent further spread of the disease.

cards.headline: Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm tease new N1X laptop processors
cards.teaser: The companies posted coordinated messages on social media ahead of an industry event, hinting at processor announcements.
cards.body:
Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm are teasing Nvidia's new N1X laptop processors ahead of Computex this weekend. The companies posted coordinated messages on social media referencing "a new era of PC," with posts appearing on the Windows and Nvidia GeForce accounts on X, followed by Arm's own announcement.

Microsoft's Surface and Windows chief Pavan Davuluri also teased upcoming hardware, sharing an image of what appears to be a curved display edge and hinting that something new is coming for developers.

hero.headline: Nationals fire executive after video shows comments about avoiding conservative player on social media
hero.body:
The Washington Nationals dismissed a team executive following the release of a hidden-camera video in which the official allegedly admitted the organization avoided featuring a conservative player on social media, according to multiple news reports.

The video, which surfaced publicly, captured comments suggesting the team made editorial decisions about social media content based on a player's personal beliefs rather than athletic merit. Reports indicate the executive's remarks referenced a Catholic pitcher and implied the Nationals engaged in discrimination based on religious or political views.

The incident has drawn significant attention from watchdog organizations and media outlets. Fox News reported that the situation has prompted discussions about a potential Department of Justice investigation into whether religious discrimination occurred within the organization.

The Nationals have not released public statements identifying the dismissed executive or detailing the specific circumstances surrounding the firing. The team has also remained silent about how the video was created and became public.

Under federal employment law, professional sports organizations are prohibited from discriminating against employees or contractors based on religion or political beliefs. The allegations suggest that decisions about team social media content may have violated these protections by being influenced by a player's personal convictions.

It remains unclear whether the Nationals conducted an internal investigation before terminating the executive or whether other personnel were involved in the alleged discriminatory practices. The organization has not confirmed whether it has contacted the player referenced in the video or taken any other steps to address the situation internally.

The dismissal occurs amid broader scrutiny of how major sports leagues and teams handle matters involving player activism and personal expression. In recent years, several organizations across professional sports have faced criticism for appearing to apply inconsistent standards when addressing player political and religious statements.

A formal Department of Justice investigation has not been confirmed by federal authorities, though such probes would typically examine whether systematic discrimination took place and whether it violated civil rights laws protecting religious freedom in workplace settings.

The case reflects ongoing tensions in professional sports between organizational interests and individual expression. It also highlights questions about how teams balance business concerns, employee rights, and diverse fan bases with competing viewpoints on social and political matters.

The Nationals organization has not released additional comments about the situation, the investigation, or any policy changes that might result from the incident.

cards.headline: Pentagon recruits troops to attend White House UFC fights
cards.teaser: Internal memos show the Defense Department is organizing military attendance at UFC events planned for the White House grounds.
cards.body:
The Pentagon is recruiting service members to watch UFC fights scheduled at the White House, according to internal memos reviewed by The Washington Post. CNN reported that troops must meet weight standards to receive free tickets to the event.

NBC News confirmed fitness criteria are required for attendance, with reports indicating heavyweight fighters may be excluded from certain aspects of the event. The UFC has released renderings showing the planned fight setup on White House grounds, according to FOX 5 DC. Yahoo Sports reported that fighter Sean O'Malley addressed potential weather challenges for the outdoor venue.

cards.headline: Teenager Joao Fonseca defeats Novak Djokovic at French Open
cards.teaser: The 19-year-old won a five-set match against the 39-year-old former champion at Roland Garros.
cards.body:
Brazilian teenager João Fonseca mounted a remarkable comeback to defeat 39-year-old Novak Djokovic in a five-set epic at the French Open. After Djokovic claimed the first two sets 6-4, 6-4, Fonseca stormed back to win 6-3, 7-5, 7-5 in the final three sets. The four-hour battle tested Djokovic's endurance as the veteran's body reached its limits on the court.

The 19-year-old's impressive fightback showcases his emergence as a serious contender on tennis's biggest stages. Fonseca's victory denies Djokovic another chance to claim his 25th Grand Slam title, as the legendary champion continues competing well into his late thirties.

cards.headline: Milwaukee upsets Auburn in NCAA baseball tournament
cards.teaser: The University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee defeated fourth-seeded Auburn in regional play, eliminating the Tigers from the tournament.
cards.body:
Milwaukee defeated fourth-seeded Auburn in the NCAA baseball tournament, eliminating the Tigers from the competition. Auburn struggled throughout the matchup, with an early deficit proving costly in the lethargic performance.

A weather delay interrupted play before Milwaukee secured the victory. Auburn coach Pat Murphy expressed satisfaction for the Milwaukee program following the upset loss.

cards.headline: Sacramento launches bid for MLB expansion team
cards.teaser: A group of investors in California's capital city has begun formal efforts to bring a Major League Baseball franchise to the region.
cards.body:
Sacramento has entered the competition for MLB expansion, with local investors launching an official bid to bring a team to the city. The Sacramento Bee reported that several prominent names are involved in the effort, though some have already withdrawn.

KCRA reported that fans in Sacramento have expressed readiness to support a major league team. The New York Times covered the expansion bid as part of broader stadium and expansion discussions that also involve Vancouver and Tampa. Deseret News noted Sacramento represents another Western city seeking entry into MLB.

cards.headline: Glasgow Warriors advance to URC semifinals with win over Connacht
cards.teaser: The Scottish side will face either Bulls or Munster in the next round of the United Rugby Championship playoffs.
cards.body:
Glasgow Warriors have secured their place in the United Rugby Championship semifinals with a hard-fought victory over Connacht. The win keeps their championship aspirations alive as the playoffs progress.

The Warriors will now face either the Bulls or Munster in the next round, depending on the outcome of their quarterfinal clash. Glasgow's performance against Connacht demonstrated the determination needed to succeed in the knockout stages of the competition.

cards.headline: Bristol defeats Bath to stay in playoff contention
cards.teaser: Bristol beat the reigning Premiership champions 21-19 to keep their postseason hopes alive.
cards.body:
Bristol earned a narrow 21-19 victory over Bath, the defending Premiership champions, in a match that keeps Bristol's playoff aspirations viable. The close score reflected the intensity of the contest between the two sides.

The win allows Bristol to continue competing for a spot in the playoff positions as the regular season approaches its conclusion. Bath's loss represents a setback for the defending champions but does not eliminate them from postseason contention.

hero.headline: Marcia Lucas, Oscar-Winning Star Wars Editor, Dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, the film editor who won an Oscar for her work on Star Wars, died Wednesday in Rancho Mirage, California. She was 80.

The family's attorney confirmed she died of cancer. Lucas was a significant creative force in shaping several influential films of the 1970s.

Lucas won the Academy Award for editing Star Wars, directed by her former husband George Lucas. Her editorial work helped define the pacing and storytelling of the groundbreaking science fiction film that became a cultural phenomenon.

Beyond Star Wars, Lucas edited American Graffiti and contributed to other major productions during a period of American filmmaking known for artistic innovation. Her career established her as a trailblazer in the film editing profession during an era when few women held such technical creative roles.

The family attorney said Lucas would be remembered as a brilliant storyteller. Her editorial choices on Star Wars influenced how audiences experienced the film's narrative structure and contributed to its success at the box office and with critics.

Lucas worked during a transformative period in Hollywood filmmaking. The 1970s saw a generation of filmmakers reshape American cinema, and her technical expertise played a role in several films that came to define that era.

Her death marks the loss of one of the key creative figures behind Star Wars, a film that reshaped the entertainment industry and continues to influence popular culture decades after its release. While George Lucas received widespread recognition as the director and creator of the Star Wars universe, Marcia Lucas's editorial contributions were essential to the final form of the original film.

Lucas died at her home in Rancho Mirage after battling cancer. She is survived by her family, who announced her death through their attorney.

cards.headline: Over Half of Great American State Fair Performers Drop Out
cards.teaser: Multiple artists have withdrawn from a Trump-backed concert amid political tensions and reported threats.
cards.body:
More than half of the scheduled performers for the Great American State Fair have withdrawn from the event. The concert is part of the US Freedom 250 celebration, a Trump-backed commemoration competing with the official America250 celebration of the nation's 250th birthday.

Multiple artists have cited political reasons and threats as their motivation for dropping out. Vanilla Ice remains among the confirmed performers for the event, which has experienced significant lineup changes as a result of these withdrawals.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remaining 2026 Concerts
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old singer announced he is canceling the rest of his 2026 tour dates due to health issues.
cards.body:
The 92-year-old singer announced Friday that he is canceling all remaining concert dates for 2026 to focus on his health. Despite his age, Valli has remained dedicated to touring throughout his career.

In his announcement, Valli expressed his regret to fans who had purchased tickets to the canceled shows, apologizing for the disappointment.

cards.headline: Backrooms Film Earns Over $10 Million in Previews
cards.teaser: The A24 horror film from 20-year-old director Kane Parsons has already performed strongly ahead of its nationwide release.
cards.body:
Backrooms, the latest feature from A24 and the directorial debut of 20-year-old Kane Parsons, has grossed more than $10 million in preview screenings. The horror film is now playing in theaters nationwide.

The film stars Chiwetel Ejiofor, Renate Reinsve, Mark Duplass, Finn Bennett, Avan Jogia, and Lukita Maxwell. The movie is inspired by an original YouTube series and appears positioned for box office success based on its early performance.

cards.headline: Erika Kirk Denies Dating Rumors After Charlie Kirk's Death
cards.teaser: The widow of Charlie Kirk responded to claims that she has moved on with a new boyfriend.
cards.body:
Erika Kirk has denied rumors that she has a new boyfriend following the death of her husband Charlie Kirk. She addressed the claims directly, saying her late husband's love will last her a lifetime.

Kirk told those spreading the rumors to go touch grass. Charlie Kirk was assassinated less than a year ago. Erika Kirk has faced public speculation about her personal life in the months since his death.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Councilwoman Pushes for Uncapped Film Tax Credits
cards.teaser: Nithya Raman urged gubernatorial candidates to support expanded incentives for film and TV production.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Councilwoman Nithya Raman called on candidates for governor to support uncapped tax incentives for film and TV production in the final days before the Tuesday election. She appeared outside Radford Studios with entertainment figures who support her mayoral campaign.

Mike Schur, Cord Jefferson, and Kay Cannon joined Raman at the event. She said the state must ensure that Hollywood remains a production hub. Raman is running for mayor of Los Angeles while advocating for statewide policy changes affecting the entertainment industry.

cards.headline: Kanye West Approved to Perform in the Netherlands
cards.teaser: Officials ruled there was insufficient evidence to ban the rapper from entering the country for his birthday performance.
cards.body:
Kanye West has been cleared to perform in the Netherlands on his birthday. Dutch officials ruled that insufficient evidence had been found to justify banning the rapper from entering the country.

The decision follows what appears to have been a review process concerning West's entry into the Netherlands. The ruling allows the planned performance to proceed as scheduled on West's birthday.

hero.headline: Judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center
hero.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C. has ordered President Trump to remove his name from the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts within two weeks. The ruling also blocks the scheduled closure of the performing arts venue for planned renovations.

U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper signed the order on Friday, directing the Trump administration to take down all physical signage bearing Trump's name and remove any references to a "Trump Kennedy Center" from official materials. The decision comes on what would have been former President John F. Kennedy's birthday.

In his 94-page ruling, Judge Cooper concluded that it was "crystal clear" that the arts complex was named for the late President Kennedy. The judge found that the Kennedy Center's board overstepped its legal authority by unilaterally renaming the facility after Trump without congressional approval.

"The Court has concluded that the Board overstepped its statutory bounds by unilaterally renaming the Kennedy Center after President Trump," Cooper wrote. He noted that in 1964, Congress deliberately rechristened the National Cultural Center as the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts.

The ruling represents a setback to Trump's renovation plans. The Kennedy Center had been scheduled to close later this year to begin a two-year renovation period. The court's injunction prevents the center from winding down its programming and closing for these renovations, at least for now.

Judge Cooper's decision addresses fundamental questions about the legal authority of the Kennedy Center's board to alter the identity and operations of the facility. The judge determined that only Congress has the power to change the center's official name.

Members of the Kennedy family responded positively to the ruling. JFK's niece Maria Shriver called it "an appropriate birthday present" on her uncle's birthday. "A federal judge ruled that President Trump and the Kennedy Center Board acted unlawfully in renaming the Kennedy Center," she wrote on social media. "The judge held that only Congress can change the Center's name and blocked the planned two-year closure."

Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Trump's health secretary and son of former Senator Robert Kennedy, made no immediate comment on the ruling. However, his sister Kerry Kennedy referenced the decision, writing that she would not need "that pickaxe after all." Joe Kennedy III, a grandson of former Senator Robert Kennedy and a former congressman, shared news of the ruling without comment.

Trump responded hours later with a lengthy statement attacking the judge's decision and criticizing Judge Cooper, who was nominated to the federal bench by former President Barack Obama. The president stated he has "no interest" in the Kennedy Center following the ruling.

cards.headline: New Jersey immigration detention facility tests DHS Secretary Mullin
cards.teaser: A private detention center in Newark has become a flashpoint over Trump administration immigration policies.
cards.body:
New Jersey officials announced that state police will take over policing functions from federal immigration officers outside the Delaney Hall facility in Newark. Governor Mikie Sherrill and Attorney General Jennifer Davenport said state police will establish a "peaceful protected zone" for demonstrators as part of the transition.

The announcement follows reports of an influx of federal agents arriving at the contentious detention center, where protesters have been arrested and detainees have reportedly begun a hunger strike over claims of inhumane conditions and inadequate medical care.

cards.headline: Bulgaria to end US military aircraft presence over visa dispute
cards.teaser: Bulgarian Prime Minister said the country will cut US military aircraft stay at the end of June.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Rumen Radev announced Friday that Bulgaria will withdraw permission for U.S. military aircraft to remain in Sofia by the end of June. The decision stems from the Trump administration's refusal to approve visa-free travel for Bulgarian citizens to the United States.

Radev had previously called for the suspension of visas for Bulgarian travelers during discussions with U.S. officials. The dispute represents a significant point of tension between the two NATO allies over travel policy.

cards.headline: Judge agrees to reopen Trump's $10 billion IRS lawsuit
cards.teaser: A federal judge sided with intervenors who said a settlement to create an anti-weaponization fund tainted the case.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Florida agreed to reopen President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS. Intervenors challenging the case argued that a settlement agreement creating an "anti-weaponization" fund had compromised the legal proceedings.

The judge's decision will allow for renewed examination of both the settlement arrangement and the underlying claims in the suit.

cards.headline: Pentagon's $9 billion Dell contract raises conflict of interest questions
cards.teaser: The five-year agreement comes after Trump touted Dell products and purchased significant amounts of its stock.
cards.body:
The Department of Defense awarded Dell a five-year, $9.7 billion contract for Microsoft software and cloud services as part of efforts to consolidate its technology agreements.

The contract has prompted scrutiny over potential conflicts of interest. President Trump previously promoted Dell's products and acquired substantial stock holdings in the company before the Pentagon finalized the deal.

cards.headline: Treasury Secretary endorses putting Trump on proposed $250 bill
cards.teaser: Scott Bessent said the bill would commemorate the U.S. semiquincentennial.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has endorsed a proposal to create a $250 bill featuring President Trump to commemorate the U.S. semiquincentennial, marking the 250th anniversary of American independence. Bessent announced the initiative at a White House news conference, stating that the Treasury Department has already begun preparing for the possibility of the new currency.

The proposal would require changing federal law, which currently prohibits living persons from appearing on U.S. currency. The White House is pushing Congress to approve the measure, though Democrats have vowed to block the move.

cards.headline: Talarico leads Paxton by 3 points in Texas governor's race poll
cards.teaser: A new poll shows the Democratic candidate ahead in the Texas Senate race after the runoff.
cards.body:
State Representative James Talarico holds a narrow lead over Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in a new poll released by Texas Public Opinion Research. Forty-seven percent of likely general election voters backed Talarico compared with 44 percent for Paxton.

The poll surveyed likely voters in the Texas Senate race following the primary runoffs. Talarico, the Democratic candidate, has a three-point edge over his Republican opponent as the general election approaches.
